In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study has provided the first estimates of the HIV-1 infection seroincidence rates among women of reproductive ages in Rwanda and that these rates are consistent with the rates of mother-to-child HIV-1 transmission in the same population.
the HIV-1 seroincidence rate in this population was 3.4 per 100 women years (95% confidence intervals, 1.8–5.0), and it was highest during the first 3 months after delivery.
the seroincident rate of HIV-1 in Kigali was high (3.5 per year) and decreased linearly over time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HIV incidence rate in Kigali was 3.6 per 100 women years, and that the first 6 months postpartum is the period of highest incidence.
HIV seroconversion in women of reproductive age was 3.4 per 100 women years.
the incidence density of HIV infection among Rwandan women of reproductive age was 3.3 per 100 woman years.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we were able to show that the incidence rate decreased linearly from the first 6 months after delivery to the last 6 month of the third year, which was consistent with the results of other studies in the region.
the HIV incidence density rates were lower than those reported for other African settings.
the seroincidece rate was higher than expected and decreased over time.
